Active cancellation stealth system uses phased array technology, DRFM, and FPGA for radar echo cancellation.
The system measures radar signal parameters in real time and retrieves corresponding target echo data from a pre-established RCS database.
Radar cross-section (RCS) varies with incident signal direction, frequency, and polarization, requiring a multidimensional RCS database.
Coherent wave interference principle requires amplitude and frequency matching and a phase difference of (2k+1)π for cancellation.
The radar echo is modeled as a sum of target echo, noise, and clutter signals.
Noise is modeled as Gaussian white noise generated by Monte Carlo methods; clutter includes ground, sea, and weather clutter.
The forwarding mode active system includes DRFM, digital phase shifter, digital attenuator, adder, and detector modules.
FPGA chips handle signal analysis, database search, waveform generation, and control functions.
Doppler frequency shift modulation is applied to the cancellation wave to reflect relative motion between radar and target.
Simulation used a coherent pulse train signal with 1 MHz modulation, 4 μs pulse width, and 1 kHz pulse repetition frequency.
Target in simulation had an RCS of 2 m², moving at 300 m/s, initially 100 km from radar.
The system reduced radar maximum detection range to about 25% of the original.
The cancellation effect (cancellaty) measured was approximately 0.51 dB.
Off-line calculation methods such as geometric optics and physical optics are used to build the RCS database with errors within a few dB.
The system's memory stores target echo, noise, and clutter databases.
Power synthesis and beam forming network directs the cancellation wave through the transmitting antenna.
The system achieves zero-balance when the detector output is minimized, indicating effective cancellation.
The active cancellation system is suitable for various platforms including embassies, power plants, reservoirs, and aircraft.
Active stealth technology is more adaptable and cost-effective compared to passive stealth.
The system design allows for modularity, reliability, compatibility, and ease of maintenance.
